text:
sam: seeing a 99.9th latency spike on ai-prod-usw2 between 02:13-02:18, throughput also dropped ~30% :frowning:
ashley: thanks, pulling perf dashboards now :eyes:
jordan: any deploys around that time? infra-bot: deploy referenced: release/optimize-batching-2026 (deployed 02:10 UTC)
sam: yep that deploy. suspect scheduler changes + kvcache heuristics interaction
miguel: logs from scheduler show repeated admission toggles. snippet:
```
2026-11-05T02:12:58Z scheduler: admission_decision=allow microbatch_size=4
2026-11-05T02:13:01Z scheduler: admission_decision=deny reason=kv_cache_eviction_risk
2026-11-05T02:13:05Z scheduler: admission_decision=allow microbatch_size=1
2026-11-05T02:13:09Z scheduler: admission_decision=deny reason=batching_window_exceeded
```
sam: looks like admission oscillation—microbatch sizes oscillating between 1 and 4 rapidly, increasing tail latency
kai: kernel selection logs also show fallback to slower kernel for sequences >1024 during that window. maybe quantized kernel hotpath not selected
ashley: can you paste kernel-selection excerpt?
miguel: kernel selector output:
```
Model: redwood/gpt-70B
seq_len=128 selected_kernel=fast_gemm_q8
seq_len=1536 selected_kernel=fallback_gemm_fp16
reason: memory_estimate>avail_kv_threshold
```
jordan: the deploy changed the kv cache eviction threshold to be more conservative (higher retention) to avoid cold starts, which might push memory estimates up
sam: combined effect: scheduler tries to pack batches (to save cost) but kvcache retention bumps mem estimate -> selector switches to fallback kernels -> slower per-token -> scheduler thinks latency rising -> admission denies -> microbatches shrink -> throughput drops and tail latency spikes
ashley: do we have profiler traces for a request that hit the slow kernel?
sam: yes attached logs below (excerpt):
```
[02:13:03.112] request id=R12345 stage=kv_cache lookup=hit
[02:13:03.115] kernel=fast_gemm_q8 step=1 time=12ms
[02:13:03.128] kernel=fallback_gemm_fp16 step=2 time=98ms   <-- big jump
[02:13:03.227] scheduler wait=42ms microbatch=1
```
kai: that 98ms step dominates tail. interestingly fallback kernel was chosen even though most seqs were short; memory_estimate used worst-case from cached KV retention
miguel: hypothesis: kvcache retention param increased per deploy, and batch packing logic takes worst-case kv size when computing memory headroom
jordan: action items:
- revert kvcache retention to previous default (ashley)
- add admission hysteresis to prevent flip-flop in 30s window (sam)
- update kernel selector to use percentile-based mem estimate instead of worst-case (kai)
- add metric alert for "admission oscillation" (ops) (miguel)
ashley: reverting retention now. infra-bot: rolling config revert to env ai-prod-usw2 kv_retention=48h->24h
infra-bot: config change applied to pool=ai-prod-usw2 by ashley at 02:20 UTC
sam: thanks. will add a quick guard: admission requires stable allow for 10s before flipping to deny
sam: push coming in ~10m for admission hysteresis
deploy-bot: canary rollout for admission-hysteresis started in ai-prod-usw2
miguel: re-checking dashboards — latency 99.9 dropped back to baseline at 02:28, throughput recovered by 02:30 :tada:
ashley: leaving follow-ups in GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/482
kai: long term: change kernel selector mem_estimate to 90th percentile and probe-based fallback, and add metric for fallback_kernel_rate
jordan: also add unit test for batching memory calc to avoid worst-case overestimation
sam: agreed. I'll own the admission-hysteresis PR and followup perf tests
ashley: nice triage. add postmortem if we want formal writeup, but small impact and quick revert. cheers :coffee:
sam: thanks all :heart:
